text:
The values of the crystal field stabilization
energies for a high spin $d^{6}$ metal ion in
octahedral and tetrahedral fields, respectively,
are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a high-spin $d^{6}$ ion the splitting is smaller than the pairing energy, so all five orbitals are singly occupied before the sixth electron pairs in the lower set.

Octahedral field: the configuration is $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$, each $t_{2g}$ electron contributing $-0.4\Delta _{o}$ and each $e_{g}$ electron $+0.6\Delta _{o}$.

$\text{CFSE}=[4(-0.4)+2(0.6)]\Delta _{o}=(-1.6+1.2)\Delta _{o}=-0.4\Delta _{o}$

Tetrahedral field: the order is reversed, the lower $e$ set lying at $-0.6\Delta _{t}$ and the upper $t_{2}$ set at $+0.4\Delta _{t}$, and the configuration is $e^{3}t_{2}^{3}$.

$\text{CFSE}=[3(-0.6)+3(0.4)]\Delta _{t}=(-1.8+1.2)\Delta _{t}=-0.6\Delta _{t}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

text:
In the following reaction sequence the major
products A and B are :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Succinic anhydride with anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl}{}_{3}$ acylates o-xylene at C-4, the position para to one methyl group and free of steric hindrance, giving A = 4-(3,4-dimethylphenyl)-4-oxobutanoic acid, $\mathrm{Ar}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{COOH}$.

Clemmensen reduction (Zn–Hg/HCl) reduces the aryl ketone C=O to $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$, giving 4-(3,4-dimethylphenyl)butanoic acid; the COOH group is not reduced.

$\mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{PO}{}_{4}$ brings about intramolecular Friedel–Crafts acylation: the COOH carbon closes a six-membered ring onto a ring carbon ortho to the side chain. The ortho position next to a methyl group is hindered, so ring closure occurs at the other ortho position, giving B = 6,7-dimethyl-3,4-dihydronaphthalen-1(2H)-one (6,7-dimethyl-1-tetralone).


[IMG]

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
The increasing order of the acidity of the $α$-hydrogen of the following compounds is :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The acidity of an $α$-hydrogen depends on how well the carbanion formed (an enolate) is stabilised by delocalising the negative charge onto C=O.

In (B) the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ lies between two C=O groups, so the anion is delocalised over both carbonyl oxygens; this is the most acidic ($\mathrm{p}K_{a}\approx 9$).

In (A), acetone, the anion is delocalised onto one C=O that has no competing electron donor ($\mathrm{p}K_{a}\approx 20$).

In (C), the ester, the lone pair of OMe is donated into C=O (+R effect), so the C=O withdraws less charge from the $α$-carbanion ($\mathrm{p}K_{a}\approx 25$).

In (D), the amide, $\mathrm{NMe}{}_{2}$ is a stronger +R donor than OMe, so the $α$-carbanion is the least stabilised ($\mathrm{p}K_{a}\approx 30$).

Increasing acidity: (D) < (C) < (A) < (B).

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

text:
A flask contains a mixture of compounds A and
B. Both compounds decompose by first-order
kinetics. The half-lives for A and B are 300 s
and 180 s, respectively. If the concentrations
of A and B are equal initially, the time required
for the concentration of A to be four times that
of B(in s) : 

(Use ln 2 = 0.693)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A_{t} = A_{0}.e^{-k1t}$

$B_{t} = B_{0}.e^{-k2t}$

$k_{1} =$ $\frac{\ln 2}{300}$

$k_{2} =$ $\frac{\ln 2}{180}$

Given, $A_{0} = B_{0}$

and $A_{t}$
 and $B_{t}$
 are related as [A] = 4[B]

$\therefore$ $A_{0}.e^{-k1t} = 4B_{0}.e^{-k2t}$

$\Rightarrow$ $e^{\left (\frac{\ln 2}{180}-\frac{\ln 2}{300}\right )t}$ = 4

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (\frac{\ln 2}{180}-\frac{\ln 2}{300}\right )t$ = ln 4 = 2ln 2

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (\frac{1}{180}-\frac{1}{300}\right )t$ = 2

$\Rightarrow$ t = $\frac{2\times 180\times 300}{120}$ = 900 sec
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

compounds is :

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The compound which can donate lone pair more easily is more basic.

(A) N is $sp^{2}$ hybridized and lone pair is localised means not participating in resonance.

(B) Here lone pair participates in resonance and involved in aromaticity. So this is weakest base.

(C) N is $sp^{3}$ hybridized and lone pair is localised means not participating in resonance. As here N atom is $sp^{3}$ hybridized so it is more basic than A and D.

(D) Here lone pair of $1^{st} N$ atom participates in resonance but  $2^{nd} N$ is $sp^{2}$ hybridized and lone pair is localised means not participating in resonance. So basicity will depend on $2^{nd} N$ atom. Due to participation in resonance of $1^{st} N$ atom some negative charge is generated on $2^{nd} N$ atom which makes it more basic than compound A.

text:
The potential energy curve for the $H_{2}$
 molecule as a function of internuclear distance is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When two hydrogen atoms approach from a large distance, the attraction of each nucleus for the other atom's electron outweighs the nucleus–nucleus and electron–electron repulsions, so the potential energy falls.

At the equilibrium internuclear distance (bond length 74 pm) attraction and repulsion balance and the potential energy is at its minimum; the depth of this minimum corresponds to the H–H bond enthalpy ($435.8\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$).

At distances shorter than the bond length, internuclear repulsion dominates and the energy rises steeply.

The curve therefore drops from the separated-atom value to a minimum and then rises sharply at small distance:


[IMG]

Curve (A) has no minimum (no bond forms), while (B) and (D) show energy decreasing as the atoms come closer at short range, which ignores the repulsion.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
The minimum number of moles of $O_{2}$
 required for complete combustion of 1 mole of propane and 2
moles of butane is $_____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$C_{3}H_{8}(g) + 5O_{2}(g)$ $\to$ $3CO_{2}(g) + 4H_{2}O(l)$

$C_{4}H_{10}(g) +$ $\frac{13}{2}O_{2}(g)$ $\to$ $4CO_{2}(g) + 5H_{2}O(l)$

$\therefore$ No. of moles of $O_{2}$ required to oxidise 1 mole of propane = 5

$\therefore$ No. of moles of $O_{2}$ required to oxidise 1 mole of butane = $\frac{13}{2}$

So, No. of moles of $O_{2}$ required to oxidise 1 mole of

propane and 2 moles of butane = 5 + 2 $\times$ $\frac{13}{2}$ = 18
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

text:
The number of chiral carbon(s) present in

peptide, Ile-Arg-Pro, is $_____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Ile–Arg–Pro is made of isoleucine, arginine and proline; forming peptide bonds does not change the chiral centres of the amino acids.


[IMG]

Isoleucine, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{2})\mathrm{COOH}$, has 2 chiral carbons: the α-carbon and the β-carbon (bearing H, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}$ and the α-carbon).


[IMG]

Arginine has 1 chiral carbon, the α-carbon; its side-chain $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ groups and the guanidino carbon are not chiral.


[IMG]

Proline has 1 chiral carbon, the α-carbon of the pyrrolidine ring.

Total number of chiral carbons $=2+1+1=4$.

Hence, the answer is 4.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot

text:
The total number of coordination sites
 in ethylenediaminetetraacetate (EDTA$^{4–})$ is $_____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $\mathrm{EDTA}{}^{4-}$ the two nitrogen atoms of the ethylenediamine backbone each carry a lone pair, and each of the four $-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COO}{}^{-}$ arms binds through one carboxylate oxygen atom.

All six donor atoms can bind the same metal ion at once, so $\mathrm{EDTA}{}^{4-}$ is a hexadentate ligand.

$\text{Coordination sites}=2(\text{N})+4(\text{O})=6$

Hence, the answer is 6.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Morning Slot
